clue.text: English student pursues landlord for cheap place to stay

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the English and student pieces are placed after the landlord

blocks.note: a host keeps an inn or lets rooms
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A cash-strapped English undergraduate chases a landlord for somewhere cheap to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel offers budget dormitory lodging, typically for travellers or young people.

clue.text: Secret hard drug grips America, repeatedly

indicators.note: something that grips holds another thing tightly inside it

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
the word just built is written out a second time

explanation.surface: A covert story about a hard drug taking hold of America, told over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4-4 count is the hint that the same four letters appear twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Hush-hush is an informal adjective for something kept confidential or classified.

clue.text: Appropriate to take legal action over mouldy balti

indicators.note: mouldy food has gone off and lost its proper form, so these letters are spoiled into a new order
the legal-action word is laid over and around the other letters, covering them

blocks.note: to sue is to bring a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Is it right to go to court over a curry that has gone mouldy?
explanation.walkthrough: A balti is a curry dish popular in British curry houses; here 'over' means covering, not 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitable and appropriate are synonyms, both meaning right or fitting for the purpose.

clue.text: Employ former partner to model after some hesitation

indicators.note: after places the model piece behind the hesitation sound in the sequence

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone hires their ex as a model, though only after a bit of dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Ford's famous early car, so model can give T.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert force or influence is to bring it to bear, i.e. to use or apply it.

clue.text: Arrive shortly before media pack

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the arrival word is dropped
before puts the arrival piece ahead of the media piece

blocks.note: the press are the news media

explanation.surface: Turn up just ahead of the pack of journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Media pack' reads as a press scrum, but pack is the verb that defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To compress is to squeeze or press things tightly together, which is packing them down.

clue.text: Finally, do call for Anne to go out!

indicators.note: letters that go out are scattered from their places and come back in a new order

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea at last: please call for Anne to leave the house!
explanation.definitionFit: Once and for all means conclusively, for the final time, which is the force of finally here.

clue.text: Drink to silly fool accepting one of minister's responsibilities

indicators.note: something silly is nonsensical, so these letters are jumbled into another order
to accept is to take in, so the jumbled letters hold the next piece inside

explanation.surface: A toast to a silly fool who has taken on a ministerial duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A government minister's portfolio is the specific set of duties, such as health or defence, held in cabinet.

clue.text: Obtain unlimited happiness

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundaries, so the first and last letters are removed

explanation.surface: Get boundless joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response or fact is to draw it out from someone, i.e. to get it.

clue.text: Wilt see with great wisdom?

blocks.note: to sag is to droop or wilt
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a cathedral city with one

explanation.surface: An archaic-sounding question: wilt thou see, wisely?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilt' reads as the old form of 'will', but it is the verb meaning droop. Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagely is the adverb from sage, a wise person, so it means acting wisely.

clue.text: Impound drug in bulk

indicators.note: in places the drug piece inside the word for bulk

explanation.surface: Police confiscate drugs bought in large quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: To impound goods is to take them into legal custody, which is confiscating or seizing them.

clue.text: A French dog has large home, good for stretching out

blocks.note: being in is being at home

explanation.surface: A French dog with a big house and plenty of room to stretch its legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncurling is straightening out from a coiled position, so the body extends fully.

clue.text: Mean to operate at my punchiest!

indicators.note: to operate on something is to cut it up and work on it, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A boxer's boast: I mean to perform when I'm hitting hardest!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb meaning intend, but it is the adjective for unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of unkind or callous describes someone lacking compassion for others.

clue.text: Left enveloped in warmth and quiet reflection, Dad's in place for a pampering but  …

indicators.note: enveloped in means wrapped inside, so the left piece sits within the warmth word
a reflection is a mirror image, so the quiet word is seen back to front

blocks.note: sh is a call for quiet
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad, wrapped in warm quiet contemplation, is off to be pampered — but the sentence trails into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 12-across for the surface story only; each has its own answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A health spa is a resort offering massages, treatments and relaxation, the very place one goes to be indulged.

clue.text: …  brother's not feeling well — in fact rough, you might say!

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Frater or Friar, a religious brother

explanation.surface: Continuing from 11-across: Dad's brother is under the weather, actually feeling pretty rough.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on sound: 'rough' said out loud is RUFF, the pleated Elizabethan collar, which is a frill. 'Rough' looks like a synonym of ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruff is a stiff pleated collar, a type of ornamental frill, and ruff sounds like rough.

clue.text: Awful Elvis impersonator's last, with Motorhead and Slade take-off getting second prizes

indicators.note: an awful version is badly done, so the singer's name is mangled into a new order
last asks only for the final letter of the impersonator word
the head of a word is its first letter, taken here from the word attached to it
a take-off is a parody, a distorted imitation, so the band name is rearranged

blocks.note: read as the head of Motor: its first letter only

explanation.surface: A dreadful Elvis impersonator and a tribute act to two rock bands only ever come runner-up in talent shows.
explanation.walkthrough: Motorhead and Slade are British rock bands, the bands' names misdirecting from Motor's first letter and a rearranged Slade.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver medals are awarded for coming second in a competition, gold being first.

clue.text: All-important sale is rearranged to include e-books

indicators.note: rearranged says these letters are put into a different order
to include is to hold within, so the jumbled letters take the e-books piece inside

blocks.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A crucial shop sale has been reorganised to cover e-books too.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential means absolutely necessary or vital, the same as all-important.

clue.text: Amulet is sadly fake

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, leaving these letters in disorder

explanation.surface: A disappointing discovery: the lucky charm turns out to be counterfeit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fake' looks like an adjective describing the amulet, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To simulate something is to imitate or feign it, as in faking illness.

clue.text: Doesn't move when corset's in place!

blocks.note: stays is an old name for a corset, and the 's here stands for is
put means placed or set down

explanation.surface: Something stays fixed when the corset is properly laced in position.
explanation.walkthrough: A corset was historically called 'stays' after its stiffening bones.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put is an idiom for remaining where one is, not moving away.

clue.text: Key defender is one who can get out of a tight spot

definitions.text: one who can get out of a tight spot

blocks.note: the Escape key on a computer keyboard
an apologist argues in defence of a cause

explanation.surface: The key defender is the player who rescues the team from trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key defender' reads as a star player, but key is the keyboard key on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapologist is an entertainer like Houdini who frees themselves from chains, locks and confinement.

clue.text: Semi-clad with wood, having various final coats

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the next word is kept
final asks for the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: oak is a type of wood

explanation.surface: Half-dressed in wooden gear, with assorted top coats applied last, like varnish on furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final coats' sounds like decorating, but coats is the definition and final picks a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloaks are loose sleeveless outer garments, a kind of coat.

clue.text: Dull pain reported after surgery

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the pain word counts only for how it is said
after puts the pain piece behind the surgery piece

blocks.note: an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A patient describes the dull pain felt after an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull pain' looks like one phrase; dull is actually the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means not letting light through, so it is dull rather than shiny or clear.

clue.text: Plant's in a better position with nothing reversing over it!

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the nothing word is read from its end
over it means the turned word spreads above and around the other piece

blocks.note: being up is being ahead or higher

explanation.surface: A plant is better off when it has nothing growing back over it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flower with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Substantial job for a tough guy?

blocks.note: a heavy is a thug or minder

explanation.surface: A big assignment suitable for a hard man.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order: the tough guy first, then the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy-duty describes something robust and built to withstand hard use, i.e. substantial.

clue.text: Chatty about time out in sailing boat

indicators.note: out says the time piece is removed and left behind
about suggests turning things round and around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gossiping away about some free time spent out on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing vessel used for racing or cruising.

clue.text: Indeed resigned to gangster being found not guilty

indicators.note: read apart from the rest of its word, in places the resigned piece inside

blocks.note: read as 'in deed': a deed is an act, and 'in' signals the insertion

explanation.surface: A gangster, resigned to his fate, gets off at trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' looks like a filler adverb; split it as 'In deed' to see the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An acquittal is a court's verdict that the accused is cleared of the charge.

clue.text: Group of children briefly and quietly embrace

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the group word is dropped

blocks.note: a school class is a group of pupils
p for piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren hug each other quickly and softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp someone is to hold them tightly, an embrace.

clue.text: Detective hides her laptop in some clothing

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, taken from the word it is fused to
what hides keeps something tucked inside it out of sight

blocks.note: a sock is an item of clothing
read as the top of lap: its first letter only

explanation.surface: A private eye conceals a woman's laptop under some clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laptop' must be split into lap and top. Holmes, the fictional detective, is the defining figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes is the most famous fictional detective, so his first name stands for one.

clue.text: Way setter worked

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or manipulated, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: The method the crossword compiler used.
explanation.definitionFit: Way is used in road names, so a street is a public road, a thoroughfare.
